youtube.title: Once the mainstream political parties are infiltrated, so to speak, by these ethnic minorities...
youtube.summary: "Once the mainstream political parties are infiltrated, so to speak, by these ethnic minorities, then it falls afoul of them when you try and generate these policies." - William McGimpsey William McGimpsey argues that increasing ethnic representation within mainstream parties could make certain immigration policies harder to debate. Is this simply democracy reflecting a changing New Zealand, or should there be a political force specifically pushing to preserve the country's traditional demographics? Dieuwe de Boer & William McGimpsey break down the week’s key cultural and political themes. 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/weekly-roundup-luxon-nzsis-and-widening-political-fault-lines #RCRMedia #TheWeeklyRoundup

youtube.title: The computer assumes the worst possible scenario of everything happening at once.
youtube.summary: "The computer assumes the worst possible scenario of everything happening at once." - Ken Turner, Auckland City Councillor Ken Turner says Auckland's flood modelling assumes blocked council drains, high tide, spring tide, storm surge and extreme winds all happening together. How much confidence should we have in flood maps built around a worst-case scenario? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/ken-turner-auckland-city-councillor-plan-change-120-ratepayer-concerns-sidelined #RCRMedia

youtube.title: RCR Wednesday Webinars - Lifestyle
youtube.summary: Join Maree Buscke and Gerry Pyves to explore the brain science behind our attraction to negative information, why our brains can become hooked on it, and the disciplines we can develop to break the cycle. They also touch on the history of psychological operations (psyops) and how information can be used to influence behaviour. 🎯 Learn how to become more deliberate about what you consume, protect your attention and avoid getting lost down the rabbit hole.

youtube.title: They want to set up legislation where the punishment's really clear, the crime is not so clear...
youtube.summary: "They want to set up legislation where the punishment's really clear, the crime is not so clear, so that they can effectively weaponise it against anybody who they deem to be an opponent." - Nathan Seiuli, Executive Director, PILLAR NZ Nathan Seiuli warns that vague laws around religious beliefs, ideology and criticism could create a system where people face clear punishment for offences that are poorly defined. Should laws protecting beliefs ever risk restricting the ability to criticise or challenge those beliefs? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/nathan-seiuli-executive-director-pillar-nz-free-speech-blasphemy-laws-and-police-overreach #RCRMedia

youtube.title: YVONNE VON DONGEN
youtube.summary: Journalist Yvonne Van Dongen reports on her day spent with the ‘wrong kind of Maori', at a Brian Tamaki led protest against mass immigration, and the apparent selective policing in response to it – starting with a decision not to allow them to march over the Harbour Bridge. For more information: Check out Yvonne's substack and the Police Joint Statement

youtube.title: CHRISTOPHER JONES
youtube.summary: Natalie Cutler-Welsh is joined by Christopher Jones to discuss his book The Palmistry of Fingerprints and his 42-year journey into hand reading. He explains how fingerprints remain unchanged throughout life and act as unique biometric markers that offer insight into personality, character, potential, and even medical and genetic traits. The conversation explores practical applications for personal development, cultural perspectives on fingerprint patterns, and the deeper self-awareness gained through this ancient practice. For more information: Visit Christopher's website HandReading.nz Find him on Patreon , YouTube , Facebook , Instagram and at Hand Reading International Purchase Christopher Jones books from Handreading NZ or via Amazon
